themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 9 this week versus a 2.0-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 350% jump (z-score: 8.08)—suggesting a sudden surge in trash/waste management failures across Central Harlem residential buildings.
evidence: 9 residential disposal complaints this week vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (350% increase, z-score: 8.08)
Spike emerged this week with no prior warning in trend data
Aligns with ongoing 'Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' budget requests, suggesting potential shelter/waste management infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden spike in disposal complaints this week? Interview DSNY and building managers.
Are residential buildings overwhelmed by volume, or is a specific facility or collection route failing? Map complaint clusters.

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints doubled to 5 this week from a 1.1-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks—a 344% spike (z-score: 3.68)—marking a sharp and sudden uptick in reported narcotics issues across the district.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (344% increase, z-score: 3.68)
Spike is NEW and emerged this week with no sustained prior trend
Concurrent with consumer complaints also up 109% this week (12 vs. 5.8 avg), suggesting broader public distress
reporting_angles: Where are the 5 complaints clustered geographically? Are they concentrated in parks, storefronts, or residential blocks?
Interview NYPD and community members about what changed this week to trigger the spike.

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints spiked to 8 two weeks ago (z-score: 8.08), representing a 700% increase from the 1.0-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks, suggesting parks have become significantly louder or more disruptive venues.
evidence: 8 park noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 8.08)
Represents a statistically extreme outlier with high confidence
Aligns with CB budget requests for 'New equipment for maintenance' at Department of Parks and Recreation, suggesting ongoing facility strain
reporting_angles: Which parks generated the spike? Visit Marcus Garvey, Mount Morris, St. Nicholas to observe conditions.
Are complaints tied to events, construction, or new uses? Cross-reference with Parks Department permits and events calendars.

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests exploded to 5 complaints two weeks ago from a 0.4-complaint weekly baseline—a 1233% spike (z-score: 9.55)—indicating a severe and sudden shortage of waste receptacles across Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 litter basket requests 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% increase, z-score: 9.55, highest severity spike in dataset)
Represents an unprecedented outlier event with extreme statistical confidence
May converge with residential disposal spike to suggest systemic waste infrastructure crisis
reporting_angles: Did DSNY remove or relocate baskets, or did a vendor contract lapse? Request DSNY records on basket maintenance/replacement.
Are residents supplementing with overflow trash, leading to the residential disposal spike? Track both signals together.

themes_detail.label: Drinking Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints surged to 3 two weeks ago from a 0.1-complaint weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—reflecting a sudden and dramatic surge in alcohol-related public disorder across the district.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69, second-highest severity spike)
Represents an extreme and unprecedented outlier event
May correlate with drug activity spike and park noise surge, suggesting broader public space disorder
reporting_angles: Are complaints clustered around parks, transit hubs, or particular blocks? Map 311 complaint geocoordinates.
What is NYPD enforcement doing? Interview police precinct commanders and park managers about intervention strategies.
